content.title: About
content.content: Cookie is a baked product in the form of small round or rectangular pieces, typically made from flour, sugar, butter and eggs. The sandwich‑type refers to two cookie layers joined by a filling (cream, jam, nuts, etc.). This product does not contain chocolate or vanilla flavorings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The earliest cookies appeared in Persia in the 8th century and were called “khurma”.
In the United States, sandwich cookies became popular in the early 20th century thanks to the Oreo brand.
Cookies are often used as a base for dessert tarts and cheesecakes.
There are more than 400 varieties of cookies, differing in shape, texture and added flavors.
Traditional Russian “pesok” (shortbread) cookie is made without leavening agents, giving it a crumbly texture.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Carbohydrates provide quick glucose for the body, useful during physical activity.

items.title: Contains plant oils
items.content: Butter or vegetable oil in cookies supplies essential fatty acids.

items.title: Rich in fiber (when whole‑grain flour is used)
items.content: Fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Flour and eggs provide B1, B2 and B6 vitamins involved in metabolism.

items.title: Minerals (iron, magnesium)
items.content: Whole‑grain versions contain iron and magnesium, important for blood formation and nerve function.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Excessive intake can contribute to weight gain and increase the risk of cavities.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑flour cookies may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease.

items.title: Trans fats (when margarine is used)
items.content: Some margarines contain trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Salt content
items.content: Salty varieties can raise blood pressure if consumed frequently.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookies can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, used as a base for desserts, spread with jam, nut cream or cream cheese. Sandwich cookies are convenient to take on the go.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cookies in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer storage keep them in the refrigerator to prevent fat oxidation. Discard any cookies that show mold or off‑odors.
